subject: Staggered discount phasing & fallback guardrails (order schedule)
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@stratushealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Staggered discount phasing & fallback guardrails (order schedule)

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Stratus is excited about moving forward. Before we sign the order schedule we need clarity on two related items and would like a proposed redline so we can move to procurement sign-off:

1) Discount phasing: we want the volume discount to ramp in over four fiscal quarters (25%/50%/75%/100% of the full rate card discount) rather than an immediate full discount. Can you confirm if Redwood can support this cadence and how it will be reflected in the order form? Specifically we need:
   - language for the step-down/step-up schedule,
   - billing treatment during partial discount months, and
   - whether true-ups will be applied at quarter-end.

2) Floor & fallback protections: our finance team insists on a minimum 'fee floor' that prevents retroactive downward repricing below an agreed per-token floor if usage temporarily falls (we can accept a short grace window). We also need a fallback policy if the model packaging or tiering changes mid-term (e.g., model deprecated or packaging consolidated).

We attached our suggested pricing matrix for reference (pricing_matrix_v2.csv). Can you send a redline of the order form exhibiting: the staggered discount schedule, an explicit fee floor clause, and a fallback paragraph that covers both packaging changes and model deprecation?

Timing: procurement needs a redline by EOD Thursday (13 Aug) to hit contractual deadlines.

Appreciate your help — happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lewis
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Stratus Health
Attachment: pricing_matrix_v2.csv (csv, 12 KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staggered discount phasing & fallback guardrails (order schedule)

Sarah — thanks for the clear note and the matrix. Laura and I reviewed with product/finance and we can support a stepped discount cadence and a durable minimum fee floor. I've attached a proposed redline of the order form that includes two options for the fallback behavior (Option A: packaging-conversion credit; Option B: automatic model-variant fallback to a comparable SKU).

High-level summary of the changes I made in redline_orderform_v3.docx:
- Exhibit B (Pricing Schedule): added Section 2.1.1 "Stepped Discount Schedule" with quarter-by-quarter percentages and billing examples.
- Exhibit B: added Section 2.3 "Fee Floor" defining a per-token minimum that prevents retroactive reductions below the floor during the agreed quarterly grace window.
- Exhibit C: "Packaging & Model Fallbacks" — two fallback mechanisms (credit-based and SKU-fallback), with a proposed 60-day notice + operational transition window.

Two items for you to confirm:
1) Grace window length — we've defaulted to 30 days in the redline but can extend to 60 as you suggested.
2) True-up mechanics — the redline applies quarterly true-ups that settle at the end of each quarter; interim invoices reflect the effective discount percentage for the billing period.

If that's acceptable we'll circulate the redline to legal and finance next and loop Karthik for final legal polish.

Attachment: redline_orderform_v3.docx (docx, 45 KB)

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0168

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@stratushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staggered discount phasing & fallback guardrails (order schedule)

Markus / Laura — looping in legal redlines below. I reviewed redline_orderform_v3.docx and proposed a tightened version of the fee floor language plus an operational definition for the packaging fallback. Please see the suggested clause snippets (copied inline for speed):

--- Suggested language for Exhibit B (Fee Floor) ---
"Fee Floor. Notwithstanding any other provision, during the Term, Customer shall not be entitled to retroactive downward price adjustments for any Billing Period that would result in an effective per-token fee below $0.0008 ("Fee Floor"). The Fee Floor shall remain in effect during the applicable Quarterly Grace Window, defined as thirty (30) days following the end of the applicable Quarter. Any cumulative true-up that would otherwise reduce aggregate billings below the Fee Floor shall be capped such that the effective per-token price for the Quarter equals the Fee Floor."

--- Suggested language for Exhibit C (Packaging & Fallback) ---
"Packaging Fallback. If Redwood materially changes packaging or decommissions a specific SKU that Customer uses, Redwood will provide Customer with (i) a reasonably comparable SKU and (ii) either (A) a pro-rata credit for any functional loss relative to the previous SKU for a period of up to sixty (60) days, or (B) upon mutual agreement, the option to elect a one-time transition credit equal to the difference in list-fee economics for the quarter in which the change occurs. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to migrate Customer to the comparable SKU with no interruption to service."

Operational notes: the redline currently uses a default 30-day grace window; legal suggests keeping 30 days for the Fee Floor but 60 days for the migration/credit remedy. Also propose an explicit carveout that packaging consolidations triggered by security vulnerabilities, regulatory denial, or force majeure will follow the emergency transition playbook (shorter notice but preserved credit rights)."

I left a few inline comments in the attached markup (we should confirm the numeric Fee Floor — I used $0.0008 as a placeholder based on the pricing matrix). If Stratus is comfortable with these mechanics I recommend we push the redline back to them with Option A as the default and Option B as "Customer election".

-Karthik
Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Markus / Karthik / Laura — thanks, the redline looks good and legal at Stratus reviewed Karthik's suggested wording. A couple final items before we sign:

1) Fee Floor amount: we propose $0.00075 per token rather than $0.0008.
2) Termination carve-out: we need a one-time cap on early-termination refunds tied to the stepped discount (so Redwood is not liable for a large retroactive credit if we significantly downscale in Q1 of the ramp). Proposed language: cap transitional refund exposure to 50% of the quarter's incremental discount liability.

If you can accept those two tweaks we'll have procurement run DocuSign and I will countersign. I've initiated the DocuSign envelope (link below) to speed things up; please process the updated redline and I'll countersign once I see the final DocuSign.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/xyz/Stratus-Order-Form-DS-12345

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to take a 15-min call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Stratus Health
